summary: This Dockerfile creates a PHP 8.2 container for running tests with Chrome browser and driver. It sets up a non-root user matching the host machine's permissions, installs system dependencies and Chrome, and prepares a working directory for test scripts.

explanations.4: ARG lets you define build-time variables that can be passed when building the image; this one sets the user ID that will be created inside the container.
explanations.5: Similar to the UID, this sets the group ID for the user — typically these match the host machine's IDs so files created in containers have proper permissions.
explanations.6: This is the username that will be created inside the container.
explanations.9: This variable specifies which exact version of Chrome to download and install.
explanations.12: FROM tells Docker to start with the official PHP 8.2 image as the base, so we inherit PHP and all its dependencies.
explanations.15: RUN executes shell commands during the build; here we're updating the package manager and installing common tools like git and wget needed later.
explanations.20: These ARG lines repeat the arguments so they're available in this later stage of the build — Docker forgets ARG values between certain build phases otherwise.
explanations.24: groupadd creates a Unix group with the specified ID, and useradd creates a user account inside the container that matches the host machine's UID and GID.
explanations.30: This is a URL to a JSON file listing all available Chrome versions and download links; we'll query it to find the right download URL.
explanations.33: This downloads Google's signing key and adds it to apt's trusted keys, so the system trusts Chrome packages from Google's repository.
explanations.46: curl fetches the JSON file, then jq (a JSON tool) parses it to find the download URL for the specific Chrome version and linux64 platform.
explanations.48: This prints a colored message to the Docker build log showing which Chrome driver version was installed.
explanations.50: unzip extracts the downloaded zip file directly into the /usr/local/bin/chrome folder; the -j flag skips creating an extra subfolder.
explanations.55: Similar to line 46, but this time we're querying for the chromedriver download URL instead of the browser.
explanations.60: chmod +x makes the Chrome executable file runnable; without this, the system couldn't launch Chrome.
explanations.66: COPY --from copies Composer (a PHP package manager) from a pre-built image, rather than building it ourselves, to save time.
explanations.69: mkdir creates the directory where test scripts and configuration will live.
explanations.72: WORKDIR sets the default directory where commands run inside the container; it's like cd into this folder by default.
